text_fidelity_a:
Vziimo Titanic Ship in a Bottle Building Set with LED Lighting and Display Case, Collectible Architecture Sunken Ship Micro Blocks Kits for Adults Age 12+ Gift, Compatible with Nano (1040 Pieces) Nano bricks are tiny! This isn’t a set for young kids, unless they are closely supervised while building. I’d say adults and older teens, due to the small size of the pieces and complexity of the instructions.

Unlike most building sets where the pieces for each step are shown next to that step, these instructions show a bunch of pieces for several steps at once. So you might have a pile of 50 or 60 pieces for the next 3 or 4 steps (or more).

The instructions themselves require attention to detail, you really have to pay attention to how the pieces are laid out. A single step might involve 20 pieces or more.

Instructions aside, the pieces don’t snap together very well. I was building the ship on a desk, but even with the hard surface, the pieces aren’t straight. The bottom of my Titanic is curling upwards even before I get to the part that’s supposed to be bent from the iceberg. I pressed so hard my fingers hurt but I still couldn’t get all the pieces to fit together as they should.

I wish the stand for the bottle was made from bricks instead of faux wood. The stand looks clunky and is flimsy.
text_fidelity_b: Vziimo Titanic Ship in a Bottle Building Set with LED Lighting and Display Case, Collectible Architecture Sunken Ship Micro Blocks Kits for Adults Age 12+ Gift, Compatible with Nano (1040 Pieces)

Crayola Take Note Colorful Writing Set, At Home Crafts for Kids, Bullet Journal Supplies, 19 Pieces This is a nice sampler pack of the Crayola pens, markers and highlighters. The erasable highlighters are especially cool and something I haven't seen before. The washable gel pens are nice, comfortable grip, vibrant ink and quick drying so great for left handers. The permanent markers and dry-erase markers offer good performance but nothing really special or noteworthy about them. I do like the felt tip pens, they offer performance similar to the conte felt tip pens with a more comfortable shape.

The only thing I don't like about this set is the silly names applied to the colors. I get that it is supposed to be cute but does the black color really need to be called 'little black dress' and 'twilight sky' instead of blue. I totally get why crayola does this for their crayons where there are hundreds of colors with similar shades that need unique names.. but it makes no sense to apply silly names to basic black and blue colors, and especially to use several different names for the same color (ie the black shade is 'little black dress' for dry-erase markers but the black permanent marker is 'always onyx').

My 6 year old daughter was reading the dry-erase marker and was quite confused why it said 'little black dress' when it is a marker and not a dress.. I didn't feel like going into a long explanation about what a 'little black dress' is so I just told her its because the people who made these markers are silly.

The individual pentagons measure about 1¼ inches wide at the widest point. My favorite shape is the sphere, and it takes up my whole hand. To give an idea, it’s bigger than the average lemon. The sphere is heavy, too. I notice the weight of it in my hand.

Both sides of each pentagon piece are faceted, so they have texture instead of being smooth. The facets make the sphere very sparkly, even in a dimly lit room.

Black+Decker Kids Workbench - Power Tools Workshop - Build Your Own Toy Tool Box – 75 Realistic Toy Tools and Accessories [Amazon Exclusive] I'm disappointed in this workbench. Knowing I would eventually want to get our boy a tool bench, I started shopping for one when he was just when he was a newborn. After carefully reviewing every bench on the market, this seemed like the best one, based on the reviews on several sites.

But here are some of the reasons why I am disappointed:
- The vice (vise) grip no longer opens and closes like in the previous version.
- the nails and screws don't stay up on their own, you put them in the holes and they sink immediately (which completely defeats the purpose of pounding them down with a hammer).
- the batteries are already drained in the saw and drill press, and it hasn't even been out of the box for a month.
- the drill press lights are too bright and flash rapidly... seizure anyone???
- as you'll notice from the other uploaded pictures, the hooks that hang on the tools (like the screw driver, hammer, etc) fall out immediately.
- the storage shelf underneath is incredibly shallow; you really can't store anything of the extra pieces down there. And even the slightest play motion from your toddler will knock everything off of the lower shelf.

So with all that said, it still gets 3 stars because our 24 month old plays with it several times a day.

And another FYI: The last two years, the mega chain store with the bulls-eye logo has put this toy on sale during Black Friday weekend for $40 dollars, so Amazon drops their price too. For $40, it was an ok buy.... but for the $60 dollars it is listed for now (or for the $80 it was listed for in the weeks on Amazon prior to black Friday), I feel like this was completely over-priced. You'd be better off watching craig's list or finding it at a re-sale shop for the equally-as-good used version for around $25-30. In fact, the older used version (where the vice grip is in the front, not on the side) would give you a working vice/vise grip; which I remember playing with a real version in my dad's workshop as a kid and it was a blast!!! (while he supervised of course) :-)
text_fidelity_b: Black+Decker Kids Workbench - Power Tools Workshop - Build Your Own Toy Tool Box – 75 Realistic Toy Tools and Accessories [Amazon Exclusive]

Schleich Portable Barn with Accessories The Schleich barn is made of wood and is of extremely high quality except for a problem with the clips and pieces of wood that hold the barn roof together.

The barn opens into two separate unattached halves that slide together at right angles like a puzzle. There are latches on either short side of the barn that can be unlatched to display each half. The barn can be left open or closed. When closed it is easy to carry. A cow, chicken, donkey, lamb, hay bale, basket, red and green vegetables, and a pitch fork and broom are the accessories included. The barn doors on the long side of the barn open in both front and back. The color is vibrant and the farm animals are very realistic.

The only negative I found is that the entire barn is held together with clips that come apart. The clips are not its strongest point. The four clips on either side of the barn roof on mine would not hold up the roof and the boards keep falling off. I tried for over 30 minutes to get two of the clips seated correctly but neither side would snap in place. My boyfriend also looked at this barn and he could not get the clips to seat firmly in place either. He did say, however, that this is a well-made toy. According to the side of the box below the Germany label, it says this is made in Slovakia.

The clips and vegetable pieces that come with the barn can present a choking hazard to a small child. If the child is of that age where items are frequently "tasted," then I recommend adult supervision while the child is playing with this barn. The box indicates that this is not for children under 3 years of age and does state that the small parts present a choking hazard. This is typical of many toys with small parts, however.

Other than this, I got this for my friend's son to play with and he's going to love it. However, he'll have to play with the two roof slats off since they will fall off in its current condition. If the unit I received did not have this problem, I would have rated this 5 stars. Since mine does have this problem, I'm rating it 3. Had I purchased this unit and not received it for review, I would have returned it for a replacement. Since the three other reviewers have not complained about this issue, I suspect it is either a new issue introduced in recent manufacturing design or the unit I received is slightly defective. If there are no other recent reviews that complain about the clips and barn roof, then I would consider this a 5-star toy where I was the one exception. Nevertheless, this defect will not detract from my friend's son enjoyment as young children rarely notice those things.
text_fidelity_b: Schleich Portable Barn with Accessories

I have spent the last 90 minutes trying to decorate this mug. The parts sent with the mug do not attach; you can place them but they immediately fall off. Those parts fit to one another very well, but they decline to play nicely (or at all) with their mug.

I tried LEGO pieces and they do not want to be pressed onto the mug. I really cannot blame them.

The only block pieces that do fit onto the mug are ones I had purchased from Dollar Tree. They meld easily with the mug and hold beautifully. Unfortunately, the only surface that will accept them is the front of the mug. As you can see from the pictures they are holding well, but the rest of the mug surfaces are...well, I am trying so hard not to be all negative and everything, but the mug is so poorly designed and sloppily made that nohting will attach at all, not LEGO, not the mug company's blocks and not even the pieces of white bread that I smushed together and tried to mold to the pegs and holes. It stuck whilst still moist and them fell off when it dried and I picked up the mug to check.

We are a totally dedicated LEGO family. We have even indoctrinated...coerced...um...lovingly brought my son-in-law into the LEGO Love. We give and share those precious bricks at every gifting opportunity. There have been times when my grandchildren are out playing with their friends and my daughter and I are still inside playing. I recently learned that the one set she would love to have is the Friend's Heartlake Hotel, but by that time it was already hovering around $400.00. I am thinking that I will make provisions in my will for her to have one.

I have a tiny ton of old costume jewelry that I use for crafting and I am going to use Gorilla Glue to cover the mug with some cool bits and bobs of jewelry. Schleich Dinosaurs, Realistic Large Dinosaur Toys for Boys and Girls, Barapasaurus Toy Figurine, Ages 4+ As usual with Schleich toys, you can’t fault the durability or the quality. I’ve reviewed a number of them, and I can’t speak highly enough of their quality builds. They are made to last, even if roughly played with. We’ve had several now for about a decade, and they look no different than when they arrived, despite having gone through a number of dino “battles” and the like. This one is no exception. One issue I suppose is that it may be a little over-built in that it has quite a heft to it, which may preclude younger children from playing easily with it. It’s sizable already, but add the weight and I can see small hands having a difficult time picking it up and moving it around, or certainly moving it smoothly. Once you move past the toddler years, though, that will be much less of an issue.

In terms of looks, it’s nicely painted (again, as usual with Schleich), with the blue cuts running down central area from head to tail tip standing out particularly nicely. The pose is as if it is about to take a step forward or perhaps step on something (someone?). The face is my one real complaint about this model. It’s a raw sort of red color, which isn’t all that aesthetic. It almost looks like it’s been flayed, or perhaps is furiously angry. And there’s something about the mouth being open in the manner it is that just seems a bit off-putting.But at least the teeth look like the right sort (I hate when one has, for instance, obviously carnivorous teeth on herbivores).

It’s nice to have a new model and a relatively unknown one at that. Outside of the head/face, which is a relatively minor complaint, the barapasuaruk is another fine addition to a great line of toys/models.

KURATU LCD Writing Tablet Colorful Screen Toys for 3-12 Years Old Boys Girls,Drawing Board Reusable Doodle Board Drawing Pad Kids Electronic Education Systems (10 inch Black-S) This is yet another variation of the "Boogie Board" drawing tablet. If you are not familiar with the concept, it is NOT a digital tablet, but essentially a reusable drawing tool much like a whiteboard. It starts off as an opaque black surface that reveals a different color underneath with pressure. So you can draw on it using the included pen, a fingernail, or anything with enough pressure really, and then erase it all at once with the erase button on the bottom. The only electronics involved is a battery that "zaps" the display back to opaque to start over. This battery should last years as it only gets used when erasing for a split second.
I actually like this one better than some of our other ones as the contrast between the black and revealed color is quite high. Some of the inexpensive Boogie Board clones lack contrast and can be hard to see sometimes, but that is not the case here. It also seems to have a multi-colored background, so as you draw or write, it feels like the color is changing (really it is just revealing a different part of the material behind the LCD). I also really like the size of it, as our other drawing tablets were small whereas this one feels closer to a sheet of paper. My 12 year old son actually finds this comfortable for using as a scratch pad for his math homework, which is a great environmentally friendly alternative to scrap paper. And my younger kids like drawing pictures on it or playing games like tick-tack-toe.
You do have to be a little bit careful about resting your hand on it as it seems even that amount of pressure will leave a mark, and sadly you can't erase part of a picture, you can only erase the entire thing in one shot with the button. But this is true of all similar drawing pads due to how it works, so that is no fault of this product. As far as the Boogie Board clones go, this is my favorite so far.

Clicformers Basic Set (150 Piece) Educational Building Blocks Kit, Construction STEM Toy, Creative Building Bricks This CLICFORMERS BASIC SET (150 Piece, Multicolor) is a high-quality building set. The pieces are solid, uniform, smooth-edged, and easily snapped together. However, the pieces aren't particularly versatile--most builds seem to use a chain of connected basic pieces rolled or wrapped around an accessory piece, or folded into boxes.

Also, the finished builds don't look much like a “duck” or a “penguin” or a “necklace” or a “truck”. It takes imagination to see the build as the thing it is intended to be. To me, the builds always look like an aggregation of Clicformers pieces, instead of transforming visually into an entirely different object.

This set includes a booklet of clear instructions for a variety of builds. There is also a sheet of stickers to apply to the pieces, either for decoration or for birds’ or animals’ eyes. The set is fun to play with, if you like building toys.

I think that LEGO sets give better value, because you can build so many different, recognizable things from the basic bricks (LEGO, or LEGO Duplo for younger children), without needing a lot of special connectors. If Clicformers offer something that LEGO doesn't, I don't know what it is. Clicformers certainly aren't cheaper (as are K’nex and Mega Blox building sets).

That project, which took a couple of months, was nowhere near as frustrating as this, which took two days (when I'm determined, I'm determined).
Note that there's only ONE bookend in the kit. The first photo pictures two, but there's only one per kit. The kit comes with glue, a screwdriver, two lights, instructions, and everything you need except the batteries to power the lights. I would HIGHLY recommend that you provide a strong glue such as super glue or a really good wood glue for this project. You'll need it if my experience is anything to go by while building it.
I also recommend that you don't pop out the pieces beforehand, but do it while building (unless you are the type to label everything after you do that). There are a LOT of pieces to keep track of, and the labels aren't printed on them. Resist the temptation.
Now, for the kit itself. The instructions are NOT the best. There's 30+ pages, and very few words. It's basically illustrations and there were times when I feel steps were skipped. I had to figure out on my own which light when where (the shorter light for the door lamp, the longer one for the top light). Things like that. It was very frustrating.
Also, the kit is made out of a composite wood and has many, MANY tiny parts. Some parts that you have to push through tiny openings and through multiple openings. As careful as I was, these pieces broke. Hence the need for a really good, strong glue. The glue was also needed to keep pieces together. There were so many times that parts fell off when they shouldn't have, so gluing them together helped to move things along.
Oh, and I'd put pieces together only to have the instructions have pieces added later, and I'd be all 'why didn't they have me add this piece earlier'? Especially when you're pushing delicate pieces together.
If you've a miniature magnetic screwdriver, use it instead. The included screws are tiny and you're trying to get them in very small holes while screwing at awkward angles. Not having to worry about them falling will really help.
There was a lot of swearing involved with this project, I will not lie. I'm not sure this is a project for a kid, 14+ or older, unless they really like kit-building. Maybe if it was built out of better material. I debated what to rate it, but since it turned out looking good in the end (with the help of a lot of extra glue), I went with three stars. The finished product is lovely and the lights work, it was just very frustrating to get there.
text_fidelity_b: Rolife DIY Book Nook Kits Time Travel, 3D Wooden Puzzles Bookshelf Insert Decorative Bookend Model Kits with LED, DIY Crafts/Birthday Gifts/Home Decor for Girls&Boys Teens&Adults (Time Travel)

Thames & Kosmos Big Engineering Makerspace | Science Kit | 22 Physics Lessons & Experiments | Toy of The Year Award Finalist | Homeschool | Learning Pod | STEM Kit This THAMES & KOSMOS THE BIG ENGINEERING MAKERSPACE SCIENCE EXPERIMENT KIT is the real deal--a fun model-building kit that painlessly teaches basic concepts of physics (e.g., thermal air currents, levers, momentum). Each model (e.g., crane, helicopter) actually works, and is accompanied by a “what's happening here” explanation in the manual of why it works (e.g., turning a crank hoists a crane load by exerting force on a rope threaded through pulleys that share the weight to be lifted; a helicopter’s fast tail rotor produces a force that counteracts the main rotor’s force to stabilize the helicopter).

The models are assembled from plastic parts (some parts are similar to LEGO Technic elements) by following clear step-by-step diagrams (similar to LEGO building instructions). They are powered by a pressurized air tank controlled by a switch with a lever. There are no batteries to buy or charge, because you pressurize the air tank by pumping air into it (the pump assembly resembles a bicycle tire pump).

Each model has suggestions for finding out more about the scientific principles that relate to it. The manual indicates the difficulty level of each model with a three-dot system (easy, medium, difficult).

This kit may seem expensive (about $90 on Amazon), but it teaches a LOT about the practical application of physical and engineering principles, for the price of a single medium-sized LEGO Technic kit. It's a kit to use in home schooling, or to give to a child who really wants to understand why and how construction equipment, vehicles, watercraft, aircraft, and cameras work in the real world.

Drone Home -- First Ever Game With a Real, Flying Drone -- Great, Family Fun! -- For 2-4 Players -- Ages 8+ I have very mixed feelings about this game. First, it is REALLY FUN, and my kids and I were laughing really hard playing it. The drone taking off is really a lot of fun and cool to see, and even our little 3 year old who is too young to play was enamored by it and shrieking when it would lift off with little playing pieces inside! Really a lot of fun.
That being said, there are 3 caveats to be aware of:
1)I don't feel comfortable letting the kids play this alone. The drone comes crashing down sometimes and I want an adult or kid old enough to be able to catch it to avoid hurting anyone / furniture, or crashing so hard it cracks the plastic (a part of the drone siding already popped out, but I was able to push it back into place).

2) I feel like this game won't last very long. The pieces are VERY easily lost, as they end up being flung around the room as you play. Also, the drone lifting off bumps into the ceiling easily (thankfully we have cathedral ceilings in our living and had to move the game over to there, otherwise it would hit and come crashing down fast). It's only a matter of time before the plastic breaks or pieces get lost forever.

3) I dove to catch it on the way down after a particular round, and it hurt my finger. Nothing major, didn't hurt more than stubbing your toe on furniture or stepping on a lego- it has a safety to shut the propeller if it detects something in the way, but I was still surprised. I was fine, but one of my kids would have been crying if it happened to them.

My daughter actually suggested we try playing it outside next time, which might solve some of the issues- can't do damage to the house and everyone can duck for cover until it crashes into the grass. Wind might make it less fun though. HOWEVER- this was a TON OF FUN TO PLAY, so even with all those caveats, and even considering it might not last more than a few months in my household, I'd still consider it worth playing even for those few times. The look on their faces when the drone takes off is PRICELESS, and worth it even if you only get to play it once.
text_fidelity_b: Drone Home -- First Ever Game With a Real, Flying Drone -- Great, Family Fun! -- For 2-4 Players -- Ages 8+

text_fidelity_a: Educational Insights Panda Rollers I work in a high school special ed classroom. The students are considered to be moderate-intellect. I took this game in to play with some of them. The game can be played with 2, 3 or 4 players. Each player gets a set of 12 "eye" cards. There are two cards of each eye color, but one is a left side of the face and the other is the right side. You have to physically pick up the panda board to shake the dice. At first I thought it was like the old classic game Trouble where you press on the dome to get the dice to move, but that's not how it works. After the dice are rolled, you find the two cards in your pile the match what shows up on the panda board. It took one of my students a while before she started "getting" that the left/ride side mattered, but my other student picked up on it fairly quickly. I ended up with a set of cards, too, and I would position it correctly and model it for the one student to copy. The first person to have the correct eye match, wins a tile. We ended up playing three full games. Both kids liked it a lot. Although they are in high school, it was very appropriate for their academic levels. There's no reading, so we weren't slowed down by that. I would definitely recommend this to other special ed teachers or people with preschoolers.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Panda Rollers

TitanShield Solid Gold Polyhedral Dungeons and Dragons D&D Metal 7-Dice Set These are really beautiful and well packaged. They come in a small, foam-lined tin. The tin is slightly larger than a standard deck of playing cards, but it fits easily into a pocket. These really are the most beautiful dice I have ever seen and photos really do not do them justice.

The dice are slightly smaller than my other standard sized, acrylic polyhedral dice sets. They roll well, but I'm sticking to a dice box or tower to avoid denting surfaces. I think the dice themselves can likely withstand denting, as they are solid metal.

These would be great for a wealthy and/or greedy character. The only real downside is that though most of the dice have a smooth edge, the 4-sided dice is awfully sharp. This could do some damage if squeezed too tightly, carried unprotected in a pocket or stepped upon. So, use some caution.

These are really pretty and would make a nice gift for any table top gamer in your life or for yourself.

Thank you for reading my review. I hope you found it informative and helpful.
text_fidelity_b: TitanShield Solid Gold Polyhedral Dungeons and Dragons D&D Metal 7-Dice Set

Pop Up Super Mario Family and Preschool Kids Board Game, 2-4 Players, Suitable for Boys & Girls Ages 4+ If you, like me, are looking for games to play with a high energy, lack of focus little boy, then this is the game for you. For my four year old, games with a lot of rules and that require skills he's still learning with clear winners and losers are not the best choice games for us. He doesn't have the patience, skill, or temperament. I needed games to slowly introduce him into those skills and Pop Up Pirate is that game! The only rule, everyone takes turns to place a sword into a slot. The person who makes the pirate pop-up out of the barrel wins. We don't play winner/loser, but you can if you choose to do so.

The game comes with 20 swords, four colors with five each, a barrel, and said pirate. It's for 2 to 4 players, my son and I just pick up a sword no matter the color, but if you have more kids or players, then you can choose colors. You stick the pirate in the barrel where there is a trap/spring mechanism that is only triggered when someone sticks a sword in the right slot. Each player takes a color and everyone takes turns sticking a sword into a slot. When the right sword pokes the pirate, he pops high up into the air. The pirate is fairly light weight so if he were to really go flying he would not break anything or hurt anyone. The pirate jumps at most 2 feet into the air, probably less. The only caveat is to make kids aren't sticking their face near the barrel with the pirate in the hole for obvious reasons. This game comes in fairly big box as the barrel is about as wide as a clothes iron, but not nearly as tall.

If you need a game for toddlers/preschoolers that is guaranteed to teach taking turns and highly giggle inducing, then Pop up Pirate is your game!
text_fidelity_b: Pop Up Super Mario Family and Preschool Kids Board Game, 2-4 Players, Suitable for Boys & Girls Ages 4+

Playskool Showcam 2-in-1 Digital Camera and Projector (Gray) For my daughter's sake, I would give this camera 5 stars. It is the longest lasting favorite toy any of my kids have ever received, EVER. I bought it for my then 7 year old daughter for Christmas 2 years ago, and it is still her very favorite toy at age 9. She plays with it almost daily, takes it with her on trips and to important events, and shows everyone the pictures she takes. I think not much more praise can be had for a toy than for it to be beloved after two full years of daily play! But I wills say, her expectations for it are different than mine. She doesn't care about printing the pictures out. She likes taking them and looking at them on the viewfinder, projecting them on the wall, and using the added features to make funny frames around the people and funny sounds. That's all she wants from it, and it delivers that perfectly.

BUT, as a parent, I would have hoped the screen would be better quality. When you look at it, it's sort of blurry and got lines through it. Frankly, sometimes it's hard to tell what I'm looking at. This doesn't bother my now 9 year old daughter AT ALL. But it is disappointing to me because I know the technology exists to make that better.

The quality of pictures is also not great when uploaded onto my computer (which I've only done a couple of times). It's VERY pixelated. Again, this isn't a feature my daughter cares about, so take that into account, but for me I wish that the option were there to print out a decent quality print because sometimes she takes really awesome shots that I wish I could save.

This camera is also super tough. Despite being dropped and thrown around and fought over by siblings for the last 2 years, it still works perfectly. The batteries last her generally a few months, depending on play. But they're just AA's, so no biggie to change them out.

Really, I am most impressed that this toy continues to make her so happy. I think Playskool could go a long way to making the picture/screen quality better, even for kids, but that's just a mom talking!

text_fidelity_a:
Pink Racer This is a fun and powerful little racing ATV that my kids, ages nearly 5 and seven, have a lot of fun playing with. We have another power wheels vehicle that we call "purple thing" because it has three larger wheels and is set a lot closer to the ground. That one, grips onto our lawn and has a lot of power for going up and down the small hills in our grassy yard.

This one, seems to even have more power than our last one, but unfortunately the tires are less grippy, so it ends up spinning out and people get stuck trying to go up a hill and have to strategize about what long and circuitous route they can take to get up the hill kind of sideways so that it doesn't lose power or more usually, spin its wheels.

This thing goes a bit faster than our other one, and has a feel of power to it, so I really think the wheels and their slippery, hard surface, are the issue. This is gotten slightly better with use over the last few months, but unfortunately is still happening very frequently when in use. We have found the issue is just as bad on our concrete driveway as it is on our grass. Our grass is a bumpy, country lawn that is generally on watered in summer and goes kind of brown and dry.

I also think they could've improved it by potentially making it big enough to seat a second, smaller child. Our other one is big enough that when our son was five and our daughter was three, she could sit behind him as he drove around the yard.

Overall, if you have a very flat, large lawn that a child would be unlikely to spin out the tires on, this is a really fun, immediately thrilling toy to play with, has a ton of power, multiple settings that are fun for the kids to experiment with, and is very maneuverable and controllable. However, for bumpier lawns or yards with some minor grade changes and hills, this might not be the best choice for getting around.
text_fidelity_b: Pink Racer

The puzzle measures 52" wide by 24" high--it's a panoramic puzzle--so make sure you have cleared a wide space for it. The XXL size means that the fine photo details are spread over more than one puzzle piece, and this increases the difficulty. The puzzle is easiest to assemble if you stand over it as you go, so that you can see the bigger, overall picture.

Ravensburger puzzles always have color areas to help you. That's true of this puzzle, but the sky--there's lots of it!-- has less color variation than usual. The border pieces are easy to find and assemble, but when you start on the remaining puzzle, it really dawns on you what a challenging task you have undertaken. There are piles of dark blue, light blue, autumn-colored, and mostly-white pieces that look very much alike. For me, the hardest area was the lower left side, with all of the blue trees; and the big snow-covered tree at the right was far more difficult than I expected. The castle was easy, and the autumn-colored trees were easier than you would think from looking at the box photo.

Despite its difficulty, this puzzle was a pleasure to work. The photo is just so beautiful! Working at a comfortable pace (one to several hours at a stretch, but not every day), I needed about a month to finish this one. As usual, I found the Ravensburger craftsmanship to be extraordinary--the pieces fit together so nicely that mistakes were few and far between. I highly recommend this puzzle for expert (addicted) jigsaw puzzle enthusiasts.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Neuschwanstein Castle 2000 Piece Panorama XXL Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults – Softclick Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly

T.S. Shure Learn to Latch Hook Book & Set This is a great set to introduce kids (as well as adults) to the art of latch hooking. The instruction book is colorful and easy to follow, with clear directions and beautiful graphics. I would give this a five-star review except for two things:

The book gets you and your child excited to start making beautiful projects (including your own customized designs), yet it provides only enough yarn and canvas to make ONE double-sided, child-size pillow. If you want to make bigger and more complicated projects, you have to order more supplies. Because of this, I felt this was more of a "sample" kit, aimed at giving newcomers a "taste" of latch hooking to get you "hooked." For $30, I expected enough material to make at least two projects. Also, what yarn there is of so-so quality - it's rather light and thin, "play yarn" for children, I guess.

Also the packaging felt odd. The book is tied to an empty cardboard box that seems to have no function other than to fill space to make the kit look bigger and more substantial than it is. It's tied so tightly with pipe cleaners that you can't help but tear the back of the book as you try to free it. Another reviewer commented that this may be due to craft stores experiencing a lot of shoplifting - but the book could have been easily secured using double sided tape or light adhesive.

Other than that, this kit will provide hours of enjoyment for adults and kids, especially those (like me) suffering from cabin fever thanks to an interminably long winter. I would definitely buy more as gifts if it were less than the current price.
text_fidelity_b: T.S. Shure Learn to Latch Hook Book & Set

Thames & Kosmos TK1 Telescope Plus Astronomy Educational Science Kit | Refractor 60/700 | Aluminum Full Size Tripod with Altazimuth Mount | 35X, 70X, 140X Power | Parents' Choice Recommended The telescope itself is really very good. Even with the lowest magnification lens attached The Housemate and I were able to see Saturn and discern the gap between the planet and its rings. With a higher magnification, things became much clearer, and even more exciting. The first clear image of the moon took my breath away.

The drawbacks? It's very hard to use standing up. I realize it's made for children, but I think a taller tripod might have been a plus here. Even sitting we had to hunch down to see anything at a 45 degree angle or above. Also, the viewfinder did not help at all. I found all the objects we wanted to see by sighting along the barrel of the telescope itself. Now possibly I attached the viewfinder the wrong way, though there really only seems to be one way to do it. Either way, we saw what we intended to see which made the exercise worthwhile.

Why a telescope? Aren't you and your children worth it? Don't you want to learn more about even our part of the universe? This is an amazing gift for the children in your life, or even for yourself. It's lightweight and easy to transport and with the help of something like Google Sky, you can figure out what it is you're looking at with ease. It's a step on the road to becoming better educated in Astronomy, and it should spark a sense of wonder anyone who looks up and longs to know more.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos TK1 Telescope Plus Astronomy Educational Science Kit | Refractor 60/700 | Aluminum Full Size Tripod with Altazimuth Mount | 35X, 70X, 140X Power | Parents' Choice Recommended

I would say the age range can be up to age 9 actually. Everything you need to make three instruments is in the kit with instructions on how to make 4. The water xylophone doesn't have any materials to make it, so you'll need your own same sized glass jars/cups and food coloring to do that exercise. Once he walks you through the 4 different instruments (only three have materials to make an instrument) then you'll start building your instrument and experimenting with them. I feel like the materials are ok sturdy; however, I have instructed my son to not play with them unless we are doing the experiments (until we are finished with all of them). We did it together with me mainly explaining the instructions and my son completing the tasks. The only thing I had to help with was folding the box. After that, we went through 3 of the 4 experiments. We'll complete the 4th experiment and then move on to the next instrument at a later date. Green Toys Build-a-Bouquet Floral Arrangement Playset - BPA Free, Phthalates Free, Creative Play Toys for Gross Motors, Fine Motor Skill Development. Toys and Games Green Toys Build a Bouquet Floral Arrangement Playset is a toy made with greenness in mind. It is manufactured with recycled materials and is great for environmentally- conscious parents who wants their kids to have some creative fun while also minimizing environmental impact. Designed for children between the ages of three and six, it is one of the few building toys that doesn't involve blocks or other interlocking rectangular pieces.

This toy involves building arrangements of flowers on a green, branch like base and there is no end to the different number of creative arrangements that kids can make. The pieces consist of leaves and three different flowers and they can be stacked and arranged in any number of ways. The combinations are endless and every time my girls play, it turns into a new adventure. My girls love creative toys, flowers, and art, so a toy like this is very likeable and enjoyable to them.

I like that this toy is made using recycled materials and I like the small, cube- shaped box included for storage. Most manufacturers do not even think about including a small storage box, and this often forces parents to use plastic bags or plastic containers to store the pieces. With an included box, there is no need to reach for these environmentally- unfriendly storage receptacles that may one day wind up in a landfill. Instead, you just use the included box, which is also made from recycled material, and the pieces will be safe to use for the next adventure.

With its lack of batteries, green composition, and creative encouragement, this toy is certainly a nice change from most others, but does it have any possible flaws or potential issues? I can think of only a few. One is the small pieces. They can easily become misplaced, so parents need to watch closely to make sure that kids place all of the pieces back into the box. Of course, the nice fact here is that you can afford to lose a few because, since they are all interchangeable, it won't prevent the toy from being used again and again. Another issue is that this toy could become boring after a while. There are those youngsters who crave action, lights, and sounds in their toys and if yours is one of them, then they may grow tired of the toy in a short time.

Recycling is certainly a good idea and creative toys that require imagination and not so much of the lights and sounds so common with kids' toys today are definitely a nice change of pace. Green Toys Build a Bouquet Floral Arrangement Playset is a very nice little toy from Green Toys and it makes a great choice for these reasons. The possible building combinations are endless and while some kids may tire of it in a short time, it still has enough positive qualities and creative entertainment value to make it worth a purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Green Toys Build-a-Bouquet Floral Arrangement Playset - BPA Free, Phthalates Free, Creative Play Toys for Gross Motors, Fine Motor Skill Development. Toys and Games

Star Realms: Deckbuilding Game What can I say? This has quickly become my favorite card/board game for several reasons.

1. It's quick. Many games can take hours to play. We play best 2/3, and it usually takes about an hour. Or: about 20 minutes per game.

2. It's variable. What flops on the first turn can change the whole game, because each player has to react to it. Each player is, of course, also reacting to the other player. This translates into a number of different strategies, so each time you play it, it ends up being 'new' in some way, even if you're playing with the same person. This variability makes it more fun because you can never just 'phone it in'.

3. It's easy to learn. There aren't too many rules, so you can teach it to a new player in a few minutes. Of course, they usually have to play several games before they start winning, but that's just a matter of learning the different strategies involved.

Conclusion: HIGHLY recommended.

The price is a bit high for what you get with this set, but I believe there will be another wave of Lego Movie 2 sets, so this might go on sale.
